version.changelog: Folders: publish.sh --folder <name|id> files a Site in a dashboard folder (created by name if missing) and reports publish_result.folder; new Folders section covering the /api/v1/folders routes and the folder field on publish, update, and metadata.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent for publishing and storage, but it should be reviewed because it directs agents to persist account credentials automatically and exposes broad private Drive sharing and mutation features.

dimensions.detail: Network access to here.now and Cloudflare R2 and selected local file uploads are proportionate to publishing and Drive storage; scripts guard non-default API bases before sending credentials, but upload/finalize URLs returned by the API are not independently allowlisted.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact ships helper scripts, but also recommends an unpinned npx install/update command that can fetch the current upstream package version rather than the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill includes high-impact account operations such as public publishing, access-control changes, Drive upload/export/delete, and share-token creation; most are user-directed, but credential persistence is instructed without an explicit user consent checkpoint.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes API keys to ~/.herenow/credentials and publish state/claim tokens to .herenow/state.json; the state is purpose-aligned, but automatically saving the account API key with 'do not ask' materially increases persistent credential exposure.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Publishing sites, files, workspaces, folders, access control, and Drive storage are disclosed and mostly fit here.now's stated hosting/storage purpose, though Drive management and token sharing are broader than the headline publishing description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with agents publishing selected files to here.now, managing private Drive contents, creating share tokens, and storing a persistent here.now API key under ~/.herenow/credentials. Prefer explicit approval before login persistence, Drive sharing, deletes, overwrites, access-control changes, or domain purchases, and consider pinning the install source/version.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Drive storage, file management, and scoped token sharing are real capabilities and are documented in the skill; this is broader than the short description but not hidden.
[TM1] expected: Folder delete is documented as unfilling sites rather than deleting them, and Drive delete operations in the bundled script require confirmation; still, users should review account mutation commands carefully.
[LP3] expected: Shell, curl, jq, file, local file reads, and outbound network calls are necessary for the published helper-script workflow, but the skill does not provide a separate enforced permission manifest.
[RA2] expected: I found local state and credential files, not cron jobs, startup hooks, services, or backdoor persistence; the state file is expected for publish/update tracking.
[RP1] unexpected: The unpinned npx install/update command is a supply-chain review concern because it can fetch a different future package version.
[EA2] unexpected: The instruction to save returned API keys automatically, without asking the user whether durable credential storage is desired, is the strongest material concern.
[PE2] expected: The cited chmod 600 command is not sudo/root privilege escalation; it restricts permissions on the local credentials file.
[E1] expected: External transmission to here.now and presigned R2 upload URLs is core to the publish/storage function; the residual concern is that returned upload/finalize URLs are trusted without independent host validation.
[P4] expected: The cited user-facing wording controls how claim URLs and local state are presented; I did not find artifact-backed prompt hijacking or hidden role manipulation.
